topic_ko: 값비싼 상업 공간 대신 무료 보도를 활용하는 노점상
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 34번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외.

passage: The steep price of land in big cities shapes how resources are used most efficiently.
In New York City, for example, sidewalk carts sell everything from hot dogs to ice cream.
With more than three thousand of them in the city, it is worth asking why they are so common.
Supplying hot dogs requires land, labor, capital, entrepreneurial skill, and ingredients like buns.
Of all these resources, the most expensive one in New York is the land itself.
Retail space on Madison Avenue rents for roughly five hundred fifty dollars a year per square foot.
Renting the four square yards a cart needs as commercial space could cost as much as twenty thousand dollars a year.
Yet space on the public sidewalk is free to vendors, so they wisely use sidewalks instead of costly stores.
choices: why hot dogs are the most profitable food sold in New York City
how New York City decides where to allow street vending
how vendors avoid high land costs by using free public sidewalks
why Madison Avenue has the highest rents in the United States
how entrepreneurs choose which ingredients to buy for their carts
theme.explanation_ko: 도시의 비싼 땅값 때문에 노점상이 값비싼 상업 공간 대신 무료 보도를 활용한다는 내용. '노점상이 무료 보도를 이용해 높은 땅값을 피한다'가 주제이다. ③이 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①핫도그 수익성, ②노점 허가 결정, ④매디슨가 임대료 1위, ⑤재료 선택은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: When we judge how a business uses resources, we should remember that the costliest input is often the one we overlook.
In New York City, the priciest resource behind a hot dog is not the meat or the labor but the land.
Retail space on Madison Avenue can rent for about five hundred fifty dollars a year per square foot.
A cart's small footprint would still cost up to twenty thousand dollars a year as commercial space.
Public sidewalk space, however, is free apart from the necessary permits.
Profit-seeking vendors therefore substitute free sidewalks for expensive commercial space.
Smart business decisions must weigh the true cost of every input, especially land.
Ignoring that cost would lead a vendor to throw money away on unnecessary rent.
choices: 사업가는 모든 투입 요소, 특히 땅값의 실제 비용을 따져 자원을 효율적으로 써야 한다.
노점상은 위생을 위해 값비싼 상업 공간으로 옮겨야 한다.
도시는 보도 노점을 전면 금지해야 한다.
핫도그 가격은 재료비에 따라 결정되어야 한다.
매디슨가의 임대료는 정부가 규제해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 가장 비싼 투입 요소(땅)의 실제 비용을 따져 자원을 효율적으로 배분해야 한다는 주장. ①이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ②상업 공간 이전, ③노점 금지, ④재료비 기준 가격, ⑤임대료 규제는 본문 주장과 무관하다.

passage: High land prices in big cities have real consequences for how resources get used.
New York City alone has over three thousand sidewalk carts selling hot dogs and ice cream.
Of all the inputs a hot dog needs, land is by far the most expensive in the city.
Madison Avenue retail space rents for about five hundred fifty dollars a year per square foot.
The space a single cart occupies would cost up to twenty thousand dollars a year as a store.
Public sidewalk space, by contrast, costs vendors nothing beyond their permits.
So profit-maximizing vendors swap costly commercial space for free public sidewalks.
The popularity of the carts is, in the end, a smart response to the price of land.
choices: 노점상은 비싼 상업 공간 대신 무료 보도를 활용해 땅값 부담을 피한다.
핫도그는 뉴욕에서 가장 인기 있는 길거리 음식이다.
매디슨가는 미국에서 임대료가 가장 비싼 거리이다.
노점 허가를 받는 일은 매우 복잡하고 비싸다.
도시의 땅값은 해마다 빠르게 오르고 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 비싼 땅값 때문에 노점상이 무료 보도를 이용한다는 것이 요지. ①이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ②핫도그 인기, ③매디슨가 임대료 1위, ④허가 절차, ⑤땅값 상승은 요지가 아니다.

passage: In crowded cities, the price of land quietly decides how businesses use their resources.
New York's three thousand sidewalk carts sell hot dogs and ice cream on nearly every corner.
Behind each hot dog, the most expensive input is not the food but the land it sits on.
Renting a cart-sized patch of Madison Avenue as a store could cost twenty thousand dollars a year.
The public sidewalk, on the other hand, costs nothing beyond a permit.
So vendors trade pricey commercial floors for the free pavement outside.
Their carts are not a quaint accident but a clever answer to costly land.
Where rent is high, the cheapest space wins.
choices: The Hot Dog: New York's Favorite Street Food
Why Madison Avenue Rents Keep Rising
How to Get a Street Vending Permit in New York
Free Sidewalks: A Smart Answer to Costly City Land
The Hidden Cost of Buns and Ingredients
title.explanation_ko: 비싼 땅값에 대한 영리한 대응으로 무료 보도를 쓴다는 핵심을 압축한 ④가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①핫도그, ②임대료 상승, ③허가 절차, ⑤재료비는 초점이 아니다.

passage: The high price of land in big cities decides how resources are most efficiently used.
New York's three thousand sidewalk carts sell everything from hot dogs to ice cream.
Of all the inputs behind a hot dog, land is the most expensive in the city.
A cart-sized patch of Madison Avenue would cost up to twenty thousand dollars a year as a store.
But the public sidewalk is free to vendors apart from the required permits.
So profit-maximizing vendors substitute public sidewalks for costly commercial space.
In effect, they let the city carry the rent that a store would otherwise charge them.
Why pay for a floor when the pavement outside costs nothing?
implication.underlined: let the city carry the rent that a store would otherwise charge them
choices: vendors use free public space instead of paying for costly store space
vendors secretly avoid paying any taxes to the city
the city government directly pays the vendors' rent for them
vendors prefer selling indoors whenever they can afford it
store owners and vendors share the same commercial space
implication.explanation_ko: '가게라면 물렸을 임대료를 도시가 떠안게 한다'는 표현은 노점상이 비싼 가게 공간 대신 무료 공공 공간을 쓴다는 뜻이다. ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②탈세, ③시가 임대료 대납, ④실내 선호, ⑤공간 공유는 표현의 의미와 다르다.

passage: The high price of land in metropolitan areas have implications for how resources are employed.
In New York City, sidewalk vending carts sell everything from hot dogs to ice cream.
Consider the resources used to supply hot dogs, including land, labor, capital, and ingredients.
Which of these do you suppose is most expensive in New York City?
Retail space along Madison Avenue rents for an average of five hundred fifty dollars a year per square foot.
Because operating a cart requires about four square yards, renting that space could cost twenty thousand dollars a year.
Aside from the necessary permits, however, space on the public sidewalk is free to vendors.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: ① 주어의 핵은 단수 'The high price'(of land 구는 수식어)이므로 동사는 'have'가 아니라 'has'여야 한다. 'have implications'는 수일치 오류이다. ①이 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ②the resources 수식 과거분사 used to supply, ③단수 주어 Retail space의 rents, ④단수 주어 절에 호응하는 requires, ⑤단수 주어 space에 호응하는 is free는 모두 옳다.

Renting that much commercial space could cost as much as twenty thousand dollars a year.

choices: ①

vocab.explanation_ko: ② 뉴욕에서 핫도그 공급에 드는 자원 중 땅이 '가장 비싸다(most expensive)'는 것이 글의 핵심이므로 '가장 싸다(cheapest)'는 정반대 의미라 부적절하다. most expensive로 고쳐야 한다. ②가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①efficient(효율적인), ③requires(필요로 하다), ④free(무료인 보도), ⑤costly(값비싼 상업 공간)는 문맥에 적절하다.

order.given: The high price of land in metropolitan areas has implications for the efficient employment of resources, as New York City's sidewalk vending carts show.

blocks.A: To make hot dogs, a vendor needs land, labor, capital, and ingredients — and in New York the most expensive of these is the land.
blocks.B: Retail space along Madison Avenue, for instance, rents for about $550 a year per square foot, so a cart's small footprint could cost up to $20,000 a year as commercial space.
blocks.C: Aside from the necessary permits, however, the public sidewalk is free, so profit-maximizing vendors substitute it for that costly commercial space.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '자원 효율'을 (A)가 '가장 비싼 것은 땅'으로 잇고, (B)가 'for instance'로 임대료 수치를 제시, (C)가 'however'로 무료 보도라는 대안을 제시해 마무리. (A)-(B)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 for instance는 '땅이 가장 비싸다'(A) 뒤라야 하고, (C)의 however는 비싼 임대료(B) 뒤 전환이라 마지막이다.

passage: In big cities, the high price of land shapes how resources are used.

summary.summary_template: Because commercial space in the city is extremely __(A)__, profit-seeking street vendors choose the __(B)__ public sidewalk instead.
summary.explanation_ko: 상업 공간이 매우 (A)expensive(비싸)므로 노점상은 (B)free(무료인) 보도를 택한다. ⑤.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 expensive, (B)는 free여야 한다. cheap/crowded/costly/indoor 등은 본문과 어긋난다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 영리를 추구하는 노점상은 값비싼 상업 공간 대신 공공 보도를 활용한다.
writing.answer: Profit-maximizing street vendors substitute public sidewalks for costly commercial space.
writing.explanation_ko: substitute A for B(B 대신 A를 쓰다) 구문: A=public sidewalks, B=costly commercial space.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 필요한 허가를 제외하면, 공공 보도의 공간은 노점상에게 무료이다.
writing.answer: Aside from the permits, space on the public sidewalk is free to vendors.
writing.explanation_ko: Aside from(~을 제외하면) + 주어 space + is free to vendors.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 수레 한 대를 운영하는 데 약 4제곱야드가 필요하기 때문에, 그만한 상업 공간을 빌리는 데 연간 2만 달러가 들 수 있다.
writing.answer: Because operating a cart requires about four square yards, that commercial space could cost twenty thousand dollars a year.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Of all the resources used to supply hot dogs in New York City, the land is the most ___________.
writing.explanation_ko: 뉴욕에서 가장 '비싼(expensive)' 자원은 땅이라는 본문 내용.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Aside from the necessary public permits, however, space on the public sidewalk is free to vendors.
writing.answer: 그러나 필요한 공공 허가를 제외하면, 공공 보도의 공간은 노점상에게 무료이다.
writing.explanation_ko: aside from(~을 제외하고), free to(~에게 무료인).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Since commercial space in the city is very (A)___________, profit-maximizing vendors use the (B)___________ public sidewalk instead.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 상업 공간이 매우 비싸므로(expensive) (B) 무료(free) 보도를 이용한다.
